thread:
sara.lin: Onboarding helios30k-int3 hitting a reproducible KV-cache divergence in long-context tests. Divergence starts ~11.2k tokens and keeps growing. Prefill fingerprint mismatch between conversion runs. Dumped layer kv indices and saw off-by-one-ish patterns in later layers.

sara.lin: Repro command below (local repro ran 3/3):
```
python infra/evals/longctx_check.py --model helios30k-int3 --quant int3 --seed 42 --prefix-file tests/data/long_prompt.txt --seq_len 30000 --dump-kv /tmp/helios_kvdump
```

sara.lin: Example log excerpt:
```
LAYER 18 POS 11234 EXPECT_HASH=0x7f2c1b GOT_HASH=0x7f2c19
LAYER 20 POS 11234 EXPECT_HASH=0x4a1d3e GOT_HASH=0x4a1d2f
Summary: mismatch count=23 contiguous runs starting at ~11200
```

emily: :eyes: interesting — that pattern (later layers, same token window) smells like a RoPE/phase scaling mismatch after quant conversion rather than pure index shuffle. Did the converter change rotary scale or apply per-head folding?

mike.h: Repro'd locally a quick run. I see the same mismatch when using the int3 converter from yesterday. If I load float32 weights and run the same prefill the hashes match. So quant path is suspect.

rajiv: Two quick hypotheses: 1) per-layer scale or zero-point drift in int3 pack causing small sign flips; 2) packing stride changed so prefill offset aligns differently (prefill vs in-flight addresses).

emily: Can you dump the quant scales per-layer? I want to compare the values before/after conversion (especially rotary freq table scaling).

mike.h: Dumped scales attached to the experiment: run/exp-71823/scales.csv (ci-bot linked below). Early glance: layer 18 scale=0.00214 vs 0.00215 in golden, tiny diff but could accumulate.

ci-bot: Experiment linked: https://ci.redwood/exp/71823 (helios30k-int3 longctx run). Artifacts: /artifacts/71823/kvdump.tar.gz, /artifacts/71823/scales.csv

rajiv: Small numeric drift accumulating across 11k tokens could produce the mismatch counts you show. But the contiguous block pattern suggests an addressing/stride issue too. Can you grep the kv indices for monotonicity? If indices jump/wrap we'd see repeated patterns.

sara.lin: Grepped: indices are monotonic until the mismatch window where a block of positions map to a nearby earlier address (looks like a -32 offset). Not random.

mike.h: I pushed a minimal converter tweak branch that preserves rotary freq as float32 and only quantizes matmuls (branch: gh/mike/helios-int3-preserve-rope). Quick test reduces mismatches in first run (mismatch count down from 23 -> 4).

emily: Nice. That supports the RoPE scaling hypothesis. Can someone run a short-turn repro that triggers the window faster (smaller seed/prefix) so CI can run it in parallel?

sara.lin: Created a shortseed test harness: `--short-trigger 12000 --stride 256` which reproduces within 30s on a dev GPU. Kicking off a CI job: run/exp-71824.

ci-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/exp/71824 (short-trigger).

rajiv: Next steps proposal:
- Mike to iterate on converter: keep RoPE tables high-precision and tighten per-layer quant scale validation (owner: @mike.h).
- Devex to add a short-trigger unit to onboarding pipeline to catch this class of regressions earlier (owner: @sara.lin / @emily).
- If converter fix passes, run a 30k token golden run to confirm.

sara.lin: TL;DR: helios30k-int3 shows reproducible longctx KV drift around ~11k tokens. Root cause likely RoPE/quant interaction. Mike has a promising partial fix; CI short-trigger is running. Will post results here. :party_parrot:
